agent_output.description: tar.gz/zip of the agent output dir (its final_answer/ holds per-vuln reports). Omit for marker-only post-exploitation challenges. Bodies over the server's upload limit (1 GiB default) are rejected with 413.
agent_output.title: Agent Output

ChallengeSummary.description:
Public-facing projection of a challenge, returned by ``GET /challenges``.

Strictly excludes flag, verify scripts, ``agent_input``, and any
``source_fields`` content. The list endpoint is safe to expose to
external callers carrying the bearer token.

category.description: Falls back to the literal string `unknown` when unset — NOT `""`, unlike the sibling `benchmark` field.
category.title: Category

objective_count.description: How many objectives this challenge is scored out of — the denominator a result's progress is measured against, known before the challenge is ever launched. `0` when the challenge declares none. Pairs with the `objective_achieved` / `objective_total` the scorer reports, so the same number is used end to end.
objective_count.title: Objective Count

objective_kind.description: What one objective IS for this challenge — `vulnerability` for a single-target app, `host` for a multi-host range; `""` when unknown. A range counts hosts it is possible to own, not marker stages: several stages can belong to one host, and a host offering only a file read can never be owned. The count above is uniform whatever the noun, so a caller reads a denominator without branching on the challenge's shape.
objective_kind.title: Objective Kind

ChallengeSummary.title: ChallengeSummary

EntryUrl.description:
A user-facing target entry point published to host network.

Only returned for ``audience=external`` callers. ``role`` is the
service name from the challenge's ``application_service_keys``
(e.g. ``web``, ``entry_web``, ``ssh_jump``); ``url`` is the
full address an external client should hit (``http://<host>:<port>``
for HTTP, ``<host>:<port>`` otherwise).
EntryUrl.title: EntryUrl

InstanceSummary.description:
A running target instance, projected for the management console.

Returned by ``GET /instances``. Public-safe: carries only the operational
facts a console needs (what is running, since when, is it healthy, where
are its entry points) and never a flag, verify script, or scoring secret.
``entry_urls`` is populated for external callers exactly like
:class:`LaunchResponse`; internal callers get the docker-internal view.

audience.description: One of `internal`, `external`, or `""`. Decides whether `entry_urls` is populated.
audience.title: Audience

cage_run_id.description: Owning cage run, or `""` when standalone. Never null.
cage_run_id.title: Cage Run Id

chal_id.description: Challenge id this instance was launched from.
chal_id.title: Chal Id

created_at.description: Launch time as an RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, second precision (`2026-07-19T16:12:57Z`). Null if the instance predates timestamp tracking. NOTE: the value is stamped when the launch STARTS and re-stamped when it completes, so for an instance observed mid-launch it can move forward (and `uptime_s` drop back toward 0) between polls — do not rely on it being monotonic.
created_at.title: Created At

entry_urls.description: Host-reachable entry points. ALWAYS `[]` for `audience=internal`, and `[]` under the default `network_only=true` because no host port is published. An empty list does NOT imply a broken instance — use `container_addr` for the on-network view.
entry_urls.title: Entry Urls

healthy.description: TRI-STATE. `true`/`false` only when called with `?probe=true`; otherwise null. Null ALSO means the probe itself errored, so null is 'unknown', never 'unhealthy'. Do not collapse null to false.
healthy.title: Healthy

lifecycle_state.description: One of `launching`, `waiting_health`, `running`, `restarting`, `stopping`, `cleanup`, or `""`. Treat unknown values as in-transition rather than failing — new states may be added.
lifecycle_state.title: Lifecycle State

run_id.description: Instance handle — pass this to `/prompt`, `/submit`, and `DELETE /launch`. Equal to `chal_id` under `target_scope=per_challenge` and for static targets; `<chal_id>_<8 hex>` under `per_agent`. Do not assume it differs from `chal_id`.
run_id.title: Run Id

uptime_s.description: Seconds since `created_at`, rounded to 0.1. Server-computed, so it needs no clock sync with the caller. Null when `created_at` is null.
uptime_s.title: Uptime S

InstanceSummary.title: InstanceSummary

code.description: Machine-readable failure code, e.g. prompt_unavailable, startup_failed.
code.title: Code

retryable.description: Whether a fresh launch (new cage_run_id) might succeed.
retryable.title: Retryable

LaunchOpRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /launches`` — a durable, idempotent launch operation.

``cage_run_id`` is the caller's stable correlation id AND the operation id:
repeating the POST with the same id + params returns the same operation and
never builds a second container set; the same id with different params is a
``409``. Everything else mirrors ``GET /launch`` query params.

cage_run_id.description: Stable caller-supplied id; the launch operation's identity. Required.
cage_run_id.title: Cage Run Id

network_only.description: Keep the target on the docker network only. Default follows the server (off on a --public-host server).
network_only.title: Network Only

prompt_level.description: Hint tier l0/l1/l2 bound to this instance. Default: the server's --prompt-level.
prompt_level.title: Prompt Level

ttl.description: Lease in seconds; the instance is reaped when it expires.
ttl.title: Ttl

LaunchOpRequest.title: LaunchOpRequest

LaunchOpResult.description: The complete, Fleet-consumable result of a ``ready`` launch operation.
LaunchOpResult.title: LaunchOpResult

LaunchOpStatus.description:
One authoritative representation of a launch operation.

Returned by ``POST /launches`` (202 while pending) and ``GET /launches/{id}``.
``status`` is a small state machine: ``queued`` → ``starting`` → ``ready`` |
``failed``; and ``... → closing → closed`` on cancel. ``result`` is present
only for ``ready``; ``error`` only for ``failed``/``closed``. ``ready``
guarantees a non-empty ``run_id``, a reachable target address, and a non-empty
``task_prompt`` — treat it as "go" with no second discovery step.

retry_after.description: Seconds to wait before re-polling (pending states only).
retry_after.title: Retry After

LaunchOpStatus.title: LaunchOpStatus

debug.description: FREE-FORM network diagnostics, best-effort. Keys are OMITTED rather than nulled when a value could not be resolved, and the whole block is replaced by `{"error": "..."}` on failure. Read defensively; for human debugging only — never branch program logic on it.
debug.title: Debug

entry_urls.description: See `InstanceSummary.entry_urls` — `[]` is normal, not an error.
entry_urls.title: Entry Urls

run_id.description: Instance handle for follow-up calls. See `InstanceSummary.run_id`.
run_id.title: Run Id

scoring.description: FREE-FORM, passed through verbatim from the challenge definition. Its shape is owned by the benchmark, not by this server, and varies between benchmarks. Do not code-generate a type from one sample.
scoring.title: Scoring

status.description: One of `launched` (fresh), `recreated` (replaced a stale instance), `reused` (an existing healthy instance was returned — no new containers), or `static` (a pre-existing target, not managed here). `reused` means you may be sharing state with an earlier caller.
status.title: Status

PromptResponse.description:
Agent-facing task briefing for a launched instance (``GET /prompt/{run_id}``).

Two forms of the benchmark's own ``build_prompt`` output — the SAME briefing a
CAGE-managed agent receives as ``{task_instruction}``:

- ``task_prompt`` — ready to hand to your agent as-is: the live target
  address(es) of THIS instance are filled in. This is the one you use.
- ``task_prompt_template`` — the same briefing with the target address(es)
  shown as placeholder tokens (the un-filled template).

``prompt_level`` is the OPERATOR-selected hint tier
(``cage benchmark serve --prompt-level``); an agent cannot raise it. Both
strings are empty if the benchmark exposes no ``build_prompt``.
PromptResponse.title: PromptResponse

changed.description: Whether any scorer's numeric value moved.
changed.title: Changed

from_record.description: True when this verdict was read back from the submission record rather than produced by the polled operation (e.g. after a serve restart).
from_record.title: From Record

grader_drift.description: True means the verifier scripts / ground truth changed since this submission was graded. The frozen verifier verdicts still reflect the OLD ones — a re-judge cannot account for that, only a fresh launch can.
grader_drift.title: Grader Drift

inputs_unchanged.description: False means the frozen evidence or findings changed on disk since the original scoring, so this pass is NOT comparable to it.
inputs_unchanged.title: Inputs Unchanged

pass_count.description: Total scoring passes on this submission, the original included.
pass_count.title: Pass Count

pass_id.description: Id of the pass just written; now the canonical verdict.
pass_id.title: Pass Id

previous_pass_id.description: The pass this one superseded as canonical.
previous_pass_id.title: Previous Pass Id

scored_at.description: Unix time this pass was scored.
scored_at.title: Scored At

scores.description: The new verdict, per scorer: {value, answer, explanation, metadata}.
scores.title: Scores

submission_dir.description: Local path of the submission record this verdict was written to.
submission_dir.title: Submission Dir

RescoreOpStatus.description:
One authoritative representation of a re-judge operation.

Returned by ``POST /rescores`` (202 while pending) and
``GET /rescores/{run_id}``. ``status`` is a small state machine:
``queued`` → ``running`` → ``done`` | ``failed``. ``result`` is present for
``done``; ``error`` only for ``failed``.

The operation id is the ``run_id``, so a re-POST while one is still pending
returns that same operation rather than starting a competing re-judge of the
same submission. Re-POSTing a finished one starts a fresh re-judge — that is
the whole point of the endpoint.

attempts.description: How many re-judges have been started for this submission in this server's lifetime.
attempts.title: Attempts

retry_after.description: Seconds to wait before re-polling (pending states only).
retry_after.title: Retry After

RescoreOpStatus.title: RescoreOpStatus

RescoreRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /rescores`` — re-judge one already-scored submission.

Re-runs the OFFLINE half of scoring for the submission produced by
``run_id``: the ``LLM_judge`` signal is re-evaluated against the findings
frozen at submit time, while the verifier verdicts — gathered back when the
target was still running — are reproduced from the frozen evidence, not
re-run. No instance needs to be alive.

Use it when a verdict is wrong for reasons outside the agent's submission:
an expired judge API key, a rate-limited judge, a judge model being
replaced. It never alters the agent's findings, and every pass is kept.

judge_models.description: Judge model id(s) to score with. Default: the server's own judge configuration.
judge_models.title: Judge Models

run_id.description: Launch id of the submission to re-judge; also the operation's identity.
run_id.title: Run Id

RescoreRequest.title: RescoreRequest

ServiceInfo.description:
One container in a launched instance.

``host``/``port`` are the address to use **for your audience**: an internal
caller gets the docker alias, an external caller gets the published host
address. The ``inner_*`` / ``internal_*`` / ``external_*`` fields expose both
views explicitly when you need to disambiguate.

alias.description: Docker network alias of the container.
alias.title: Alias

external_port.description: Host-published port. Always present; null when nothing was published — which is the DEFAULT (`network_only=true`), not an error.
external_port.title: External Port

host.description: Address for the caller's audience — docker alias (internal) or the published host IP (external). Null if unresolved.
host.title: Host

inner_ip.description: Docker-internal IPv4, resolved AFTER the health check. Null while the instance is still starting, or if resolution failed.
inner_ip.title: Inner Ip

internal_port.description: Port inside the container. Always present; null if undeclared.
internal_port.title: Internal Port

ip.description: Container IPv4 on the isolated docker network.
ip.title: Ip

protocol.description: One of `tcp`, `udp`, `http`, or null. Null for dependency services that declare no protocol. Web-category targets are promoted to `http` after the health check, so this can differ from the value a challenge file declares.
protocol.title: Protocol

service_name.description: Service key from the challenge definition.
service_name.title: Service Name

ServiceInfo.title: ServiceInfo

container_logs.description: Container logs captured just before purge, for audit. Entries are NOT uniform: the normal shape is `{name, service, status, exit_code, error, logs}`, but an entry that failed to collect carries only `{name, error}` — no `logs`/`status`/`exit_code`. Access by `.get()`, not by index. Empty when the instance was already gone.
container_logs.title: Container Logs

status.description: Always the literal `stopped` — INCLUDING the no-op case where no such instance existed. Not a success/failure discriminator; read `message` to tell the two apart.
status.title: Status

SubmitResponse.description:
Verdict for a serve-only submission, returned by ``POST /submit/{run_id}``.

The server gathered live evidence against the still-running instance and
scored the submission with the challenge's benchmark scorer. ``scores`` maps
each scorer name to ``{value, answer, explanation, metadata}``. ``run_dir``
is the ``.cage_runs`` path the verdict was persisted to — the same tree the
cage inspector renders, so a submission is inspectable exactly like a
cage-run trial. ``closed`` reports whether the instance was torn down after
scoring (``?close=true``).

**One submission per instance.** The score is locked in on the first submit;
a repeat call for the same ``run_id`` returns that recorded verdict unchanged
with ``already_submitted=true`` (an agent cannot resubmit to fish for a
pass). To make another attempt, launch a fresh instance.

already_submitted.description: True when this is a replay of a previously locked-in verdict.
already_submitted.title: Already Submitted

benchmark_module.description: Filesystem path of the scoring module, for audit.
benchmark_module.title: Benchmark Module

closed.description: Whether the instance was torn down after scoring (`?close=true`). On the `already_submitted=true` replay path this is always `false` even if the FIRST submit did close the instance — check `GET /instances` if you need the real current state.
closed.title: Closed

scores.description: Maps scorer name to `{value, answer, explanation, metadata}`. `value` is normally a float, but a scorer may return `bool`/`int`/null and nothing coerces it — compare numerically, do not assume float. `metadata` is free-form, and a custom scorer may add keys beyond the four listed.
scores.title: Scores

status.description: Always the literal `scored`. Not a discriminator — a scored FAIL and a scored PASS both report `scored`. Read `scores[*].value` for the verdict.
status.title: Status

SubmitResponse.title: SubmitResponse

info.description:
Serve (PULL) mode: an external agent lists challenges, launches an isolated target instance, attacks it, and submits its output for scoring — with no Cage-managed agent runtime.

Endpoints are audience-gated: loopback callers are internal; non-loopback callers need `Authorization: Bearer <token>` when the server was started with `--external-token`.

See `docs/serve-external-audience.md` in the Cage repo for the narrative contract, deployment model and worked examples.
info.title: Cage target server

get.description:
List challenges with public-safe metadata only.

Strictly excludes flag, verify scripts, ``agent_input``, and any
``source_fields`` content. ``entry_service_count`` is the number of
user-facing entry services (web challenges declare them as
``application_service_keys``, post-exploitation ranges as ``entry_services``):
1 for a single-entry web challenge, 2+ for a multi-entry range.

``objective_count`` is what a result is scored out of, available here BEFORE
anything is launched, with ``objective_kind`` naming the unit
(``vulnerability`` / ``marker``). It is the same number the scorer later
reports as ``objective_total``. Note that it is NOT ``entry_service_count``:
a range can publish more entry services than it has objectives.

Authentication is the same as ``/launch``: loopback OR bearer token.

List every target instance this server currently has running.

The management view the launch/stop API always lacked: without it a
console can start and kill targets but never *see* what is up. Public-safe
(no flag / verify / scoring secret) and audience-gated exactly like
``/challenges`` and ``/launch``.

delete.description:
Stop and clean up exactly one running challenge target.

``run_id`` is mandatory. A DELETE that didn't carry it used to fall
through to ``cleanup_instance(chal_id, run_id=None)`` which, combined
with the registry's old chal_id-fallback lookup, silently destroyed
*some other agent's* per_agent instance. Both halves of that bug have
been removed: registry helpers are now strict-key-only, and this
endpoint refuses calls that don't name a specific instance.

post.description:
Accept a launch as a durable async operation — the orchestration-safe path.

Provisioning (minutes for a multi-host range) runs in the background; this
returns immediately. The operation id is ``cage_run_id``, so the call is
idempotent: a repeat with the same params returns the same operation and
never builds a second container set (``202`` while pending, ``200`` with the
terminal representation once ready/failed/closed); a repeat with different
params is ``409``. Poll ``status_url`` (honouring ``Retry-After``) until
``ready`` — which guarantees a non-empty ``run_id``, a reachable target
address, and a non-empty ``task_prompt``. See ``GET /launches/{id}``.

delete.description:
Idempotently cancel + tear down a launch operation.

Works in ``queued``, ``starting``, and ``ready`` — crucially even before an
internal ``run_id`` exists (the case the ``run_id``-keyed ``DELETE /launch``
cannot handle): teardown also purges any docker resources tagged with this
``cage_run_id``. Reaches ``closed`` only once containers/networks are
confirmed gone.

When cleanup cannot finish in the request — a provisioning worker is still
in flight, or a first teardown left resources behind — this returns ``202``
with ``status=closing``; poll the status URL (honouring ``Retry-After``)
until ``200`` with ``status=closed``. Repeating it is idempotent throughout.

get.description:
The one authoritative representation of a launch operation.

``status`` walks ``queued → starting → ready | failed`` (and ``… → closing →
closed`` on cancel). While pending, ``200`` carries ``status`` +
``retry_after``; a terminal *operation* failure is still ``200`` with
``status=failed`` (the query itself succeeded). Only auth/'"unknown id"'
are non-200 (401/404). A ``ready`` body carries the full ``result``.

The agent-facing task briefing for a launched instance.

An external agent needs the same task framing a CAGE-managed agent gets —
what to exploit, the live target address(es), and the ``final_answer`` output
contract. This renders the challenge's own ``build_prompt`` against the
running instance (so target/entry hosts are the ones the agent will reach),
at the hint tier bound to the instance at ``/launch`` (``?prompt_level=``,
defaulting to the server's ``--prompt-level``). Returns both the ready-to-use
``task_prompt`` (target filled in) and the un-filled ``task_prompt_template``.
Audience-gated like ``/launch`` and ``/submit``.

post.description:
Re-judge an already-scored submission, offline, as a background operation.

Scoring a submission has two halves. The verifier half ran against the live
target and is frozen on disk; the ``LLM_judge`` half is a model call, and a
model call can fail for reasons that say nothing about the agent — an
expired key, a rate limit, a model swapped out. This re-runs the judge half
over the frozen inputs and appends the result as a new scoring pass.

No instance needs to be alive: the findings and the verifier evidence were
persisted at submit time precisely so this could happen later.

The agent-facing "one submission per instance" rule is untouched — this
changes no findings, only how they were judged. Every pass is retained, and
the response reports ``grader_drift`` when the verifier scripts themselves
have changed since grading, because no re-judge can account for that.

get.description:
Authoritative status of a re-judge.

With no operation in flight, this answers from the submission record itself
— the durable truth about which pass is canonical — so a serve restart, or a
query long after the work finished, still gets a real answer instead of
"unknown operation". Such a result is flagged ``from_record``.

post.description:
Score one submission against a still-running serve-only instance.

Closes the PULL benchmark loop: the agent launched an isolated instance,
attacked it, and (for web) produced a ``final_answer/`` output — omit the
upload entirely for marker-only post-exploitation ranges, which are scored
from live target state. This gathers LIVE evidence against the still-up
target and scores it with the challenge's benchmark scorer, writing a
serve-native submission record under ``.cage_serve``. Gather needs the
target alive, so scoring runs before any ``?close=true`` teardown.
Audience-gated like ``/launch``.

**One submission per instance.** The verdict is locked in on the first call;
a repeat for the same ``run_id`` returns it unchanged (``already_submitted``)
so an agent cannot resubmit to fish for a pass. Launch a fresh instance for
another attempt.

parameters.description: Tear the instance down (DELETE) after scoring. Default: keep it up (e.g. for inspection). One submission per instance either way.
parameters.name: close

schema.title: Close
